title: Kernel execution attribution and span harmonization for deterministic NVTX->trace mapping
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a deterministic mapping layer that ties NVTX ranges and CUDA kernel invocations to our distributed trace spans and per-kernel metrics so we can attribute latency and resource utilization to specific runtime decisions (kernel selection, attention variant, prefill vs decode scheduling). This ticket implements a harmonized naming and tagging scheme, a lightweight sampling strategy to minimize overhead, and exporter changes to surface per-kernel histograms and cold-start counts in Prometheus/OTLP dashboards. The goal is actionable signal for optimizer work (kernel selector heuristics, attention path choices) while keeping telemetry overhead <1% p99 tail latency on production-like workloads.
acceptance_criteria: NVTX ranges are emitted with stable ids that correlate 1:1 with trace span ids for both prefill and decode phases
Per-kernel labels are standardized: kernel_name, kernel_variant, stream_index, phase (prefill|decode), selection_reason
Prometheus metrics: kernel_latency_histogram and kernel_invocation_count present per model family and variant
OTLP traces contain span attributes for kernel attribution and a link to the corresponding NVTX range id
End-to-end overhead measured <1% p99 latency increase on representative perf harness for 2k token workloads
Dashboards updated: kernel-attribution breakdown and scheduler hotpath heatmap; links added to runbook
notes: We should avoid adding large proto fields to every request; use a compact integer id mapping and exporter-side enrichment where possible.
Decision: use 16-bit stable ids for NVTX range tagging to keep overhead low; reconcile in collector with model/version context.
Trade-off: Full per-kernel histograms per-request are expensive; use aggregated histograms with label cardinality limited to kernel_variant and phase.
Follow-up: consider a higher-sample-rate debug mode for reproducing tail anomalies in CI/perf lab.
